title: See and Develop People
body: Notice one skill a teammate wants to develop.
notes: Open with a new club volunteer learning setup.
aria: See and Develop People. Notice one skill a teammate wants to develop.

title: Who you can help
body: A teammate or new coworker can benefit from a small offer of help.
notes: Use peer relationships as well as formal roles.
aria: Who you can help. A teammate or new coworker can benefit from a small offer of help.

title: Your People
body: Part II draws here on Chapters 10, 11 and 12.
notes: Identify these as confirmed references.
aria: Your People. Part II draws here on Chapters 10, 11 and 12.

title: Why notice growth?
body: Someone who is only assigned chores may never get to try a new task.
notes: Compare two ways to staff a project table.
aria: Why notice growth?. Someone who is only assigned chores may never get to try a new task.

title: Activity: choose a person or role
body: Use initials or a fictional newcomer for your private plan.
notes: Avoid storing another person's details.
aria: Activity: choose a person or role. Use initials or a fictional newcomer for your private plan.

title: Can They Change?
body: Chapter 10 looks at humility, effort and coachability.
notes: Assess behaviors across opportunities. [BRENEN EXCERPT: 2–4 sentences from the mapped chapter, approved by Brenen]
aria: Can They Change?. Chapter 10 looks at humility, effort and coachability.

title: Humility
body: A teammate can acknowledge a miss and hear a specific correction.
notes: Distinguish a nervous reaction from a pattern.
aria: Humility. A teammate can acknowledge a miss and hear a specific correction.

title: Effort
body: Check what the person tries across several practices.
notes: Ask what resources and opportunities they had.
aria: Effort. Check what the person tries across several practices.

title: Coachability
body: Look for a change in the next attempt after feedback.
notes: Compare agreeing with applying a suggestion.
aria: Coachability. Look for a change in the next attempt after feedback.

title: Fair observation
body: One rough afternoon is too little evidence for a label.
notes: Discuss missing context privately.
aria: Fair observation. One rough afternoon is too little evidence for a label.

title: Activity: compare two teammates
body: One asks for help and retries. One agrees politely but repeats a step unchanged.
notes: List observations and possible questions for each.
aria: Activity: compare two teammates. One asks for help and retries.

title: Where help goes next
body: Match the time you can offer to the person's willingness to practice.
notes: Avoid turning a present choice into a permanent judgment. [BRENEN MAP] Official theme from the published site/templates, but no chapter number/title is confirmed. Brenen will map this lesson to the actual chapter before the paid version ships. Do not invent a title.
aria: Where help goes next. Match the time you can offer to the person's willingness to practice.

title: What do they want to become?
body: Chapter 11 asks you to learn the person's goal directly.
notes: One student might want to teach while another wants to build. [BRENEN EXCERPT: 2–4 sentences from the mapped chapter, approved by Brenen]
aria: What do they want to become?. Chapter 11 asks you to learn the person's goal directly.

title: Questions that open the conversation
body: Ask which task they want to try and what would help them practice.
notes: Compare this with guessing their career or probing family circumstances.
aria: Questions that open the conversation. Ask which task they want to try and what would help them practice.

title: Activity: prepare three questions
body: Write one about a goal, one about prior practice and one about support.
notes: Read them aloud as a peer.
aria: Activity: prepare three questions. Write one about a goal, one about prior practice and one about support.

title: Four possible motives
body: Chapter 12 names money, growth, belonging and stability.
notes: Ask which matters now rather than assigning a type. [BRENEN EXCERPT: 2–4 sentences from the mapped chapter, approved by Brenen]
aria: Four possible motives. Chapter 12 names money, growth, belonging and stability.

title: Motives in student life
body: A steady schedule can matter more than an extra responsibility.
notes: Compare predictable hours with a chance to learn a skill.
aria: Motives in student life. A steady schedule can matter more than an extra responsibility.

title: Mid-quiz: three decisions
body: Identify a Chapter 10 behavior, choose a goal question and interpret a stated motive.
notes: Use three separate scenarios.
aria: Mid-quiz: three decisions. Identify a Chapter 10 behavior, choose a goal question and interpret a stated motive.

title: Direct feedback with care
body: Describe a behavior while leaving room to hear the person's explanation.
notes: A private invitation makes feedback easier to use. [BRENEN MAP] Official theme from the published site/templates, but no chapter number/title is confirmed. Brenen will map this lesson to the actual chapter before the paid version ships. Do not invent a title.
aria: Direct feedback with care. Describe a behavior while leaving room to hear the person's explanation.

title: Facts, impact and request
body: State what happened, what it affected and what you are asking for. Invite a reply.
notes: Write an opening sentence together.
aria: Facts, impact and request. State what happened, what it affected and what you are asking for.

title: A club discussion
body: A member cuts in twice. Ask them privately to let each speaker finish.
notes: Contrast with a sarcastic group message.
aria: A club discussion. A member cuts in twice.

title: Screen recording: a check-in
body: Plan an 8–12 minute role-play with an annotated five-minute conversation.
notes: Script the opening, goal question, observation and agreed practice.
aria: Screen recording: a check-in. Plan an 8–12 minute role-play with an annotated five-minute conversation.

title: A student development tracker
body: Record observations, the person's stated goal and your own next action.
notes: Adapt the official tool without importing its HR scoring. [BRENEN MAP] Official theme from the published site/templates, but no chapter number/title is confirmed. Brenen will map this lesson to the actual chapter before the paid version ships. Do not invent a title.
aria: A student development tracker. Record observations, the person's stated goal and your own next action.

title: Activity: fill the tracker
body: Use a fictional teammate to check humility, effort and coachability.
notes: Include the Chapter 11 question and your own commitment.
aria: Activity: fill the tracker. Use a fictional teammate to check humility, effort and coachability.

title: If practice is declined
body: Keep the standard and leave a respectful way back into practice.
notes: Separate declining help from someone's worth.
aria: If practice is declined. Keep the standard and leave a respectful way back into practice.

title: Keep the plan private
body: Use roles and your own actions on a local worksheet.
notes: Never circulate notes about a classmate.
aria: Keep the plan private. Use roles and your own actions on a local worksheet.

title: A true training bullet
body: Name the task you actually showed someone and an observed result.
notes: Remove unsupported claims about a teammate's performance.
aria: A true training bullet. Name the task you actually showed someone and an observed result.

title: Worksheet: One Person I Will Help This Month
body: Take three questions, a motive and one next step into your next check-in.
notes: Use a local one-page tracker.
aria: Worksheet: One Person I Will Help This Month. Take three questions, a motive and one next step into your next check-in.

title: Common traps
body: Notice favorites, gossip and vague reassurance.
notes: Rewrite one example as a question or factual observation.
aria: Common traps. Notice favorites, gossip and vague reassurance.

title: What the three chapters contribute
body: Observe behavior, ask about goals and listen for motives.
notes: Have learners explain the order in their words.
aria: What the three chapters contribute. Observe behavior, ask about goals and listen for motives.

title: Next: the shared environment
body: Shift attention from one person to what a newcomer sees in a room.
notes: Introduce the coming Set the Stage class.
aria: Next: the shared environment. Shift attention from one person to what a newcomer sees in a room.

title: Optional completion line
body: Preview the completion record or a practiced skill.
notes: Do not imply that a fictional teammate was trained.
aria: Optional completion line. Preview the completion record or a practiced skill.

title: End question: humility or coachability?
body: Compare acknowledging a mistake with using feedback on the next try.
notes: Ask which behavior the evidence supports.
aria: End question: humility or coachability?. Compare acknowledging a mistake with using feedback on the next try.

title: End question: feedback in action
body: Find the second attempt that shows a change.
notes: Do not give credit for a nod alone.
aria: End question: feedback in action. Find the second attempt that shows a change.

title: End question: a respectful goal question
body: Select a private question that invites a real preference.
notes: Explain why guessing is weaker.
aria: End question: a respectful goal question. Select a private question that invites a real preference.

title: End question: which motive?
body: A student asks for predictable shifts. Identify the motive suggested.
notes: Check the interpretation with the student.
aria: End question: which motive?. A student asks for predictable shifts.

title: End question: useful feedback
body: Pick a factual line with a clear request and room to respond.
notes: Use a club interruption example.
aria: End question: useful feedback. Pick a factual line with a clear request and room to respond.

title: Answer review
body: Explain all five choices and allow retry.
notes: Four correct completes the future class.
aria: Answer review. Explain all five choices and allow retry.

title: Schedule one conversation
body: Write a role, a time and one opening question.
notes: Keep it private and realistic.
aria: Schedule one conversation. Write a role, a time and one opening question.

title: One next action
body: After the conversation, record the one thing you agreed to do.
notes: Return to the worksheet in a month.
aria: One next action. After the conversation, record the one thing you agreed to do.
